app.name: Should You Open This?
app.tagline: Before you open a shop, with your own address and numbers: will it work or not?
app.disclaimer: This analysis is a decision-support tool, not investment advice. The figures rely on your inputs and sample data; talk to your accountant before you decide.

home.sampleNote: This result uses the sample figures from the video.
home.never: Does not pay back within 60 months
home.newHint: Pick a business type and one of the examples from the video. The figures start from the example; then you enter your own data and everything updates instantly.
home.localNote: For now your analysis is stored on this device, in this browser. It moves to the cloud once you have an account.
home.quickHint: Start with the 10-question quick analysis, then move to the detailed mode.

wb.sampleNote: Figures, competitors and location data are illustrative. Enter your own data and everything updates instantly.
wb.resetConfirm: All your changes will be cleared and the example data restored. Are you sure?
wb.notFound: This analysis was not found on this device.
wb.name: Name

finance.itemsHintProduct: The first row is your signature product: competitor prices are compared against it.
finance.itemsHintService: The first row is your signature service: competitor prices are compared against it.
finance.mixWarn: Shares add up to {sum}%. They should total 100%; the math rescales them.
finance.rampHint: The first months run below base sales. The model works out how many months sales take to reach the base case and applies price, cost, rent and wage increases month by month.
finance.taxHint: Sales and costs carry real-world deductions: tax in price, card and delivery-app fees, waste, rent withholding, employer payroll taxes, profit tax, loan payments and depreciation.
finance.loanNote: The loan amount comes from the own-money share on the Location tab.
finance.missingFin: These fields are empty and count as 0 until you fill them in: {fields}.

why.negativeMargin: Every sale loses money: price is below unit cost. Fix pricing or cost first.
why.capacity: Break-even needs more clients than the shop can physically serve. This setup cannot turn a profit.
why.belowBreakEven: Your base case ({base}/day) sits below break-even ({be}/day). These numbers lose money every month.
why.thinMargin: The base case clears break-even, but barely ({base} vs {be}/day). A small dip turns it into a loss.
why.longPayback: It turns a profit, but the investment takes {months} months to come back. Your capital stays tied up a long time.
why.go: The base case runs {margin}% above break-even and the investment pays back in about {months} months.
why.permitBlocked: This business cannot be permitted at this address. However good the numbers look, you cannot open here.
why.locationFlags: The location has several red flags: {flags}. Whatever the numbers say, do not open in this space.
why.locationFlag: The numbers work, but the location has a red flag: {flag}.
why.alsoFlag: The location also has a red flag: {flag}.

flag.foot: foot traffic is too thin for break-even
flag.rent: rent eats too much of sales
flag.founder: the founder’s financial cushion is weak

pill.loc: {count, plural, =0 {Location: no red flags} one {Location: # red flag} other {Location: # red flags}}

result.beNote: {month} a month, loan payment included. Below this, cash drains.
result.capNote: Service work needs {pct}% of capacity filled (max {max}/day).
result.projHint: Base case, including ramp, increases, taxes and the loan.
result.fixedM: Monthly fixed costs (incl. payroll tax, withholding)
result.baseNet: Base monthly cash (pre-tax, after loan payment)
result.q1: Will this location really bring {be}+ {unit} a day? Count the people walking past the door for a full week.
result.q2: Can you fund {invest} in total, including the working capital that carries the first loss-making months?
result.q3: What is the one thing you will do that nearby competitors don’t?

area.areaHint: The address you are considering and the population within a 1 km radius.
area.demoHint: The demand side: who lives here, what they earn, who passes by during the day. Income and age feed the demand-fit score and the pricing call.
area.incHint: Enter both incomes for the same period (both monthly or both annual); the math only uses the ratio between them.
area.elecHint: Not scored. In a later phase it goes to the Claude analysis only as local context.
area.lElec: Result summary (e.g. top two and their shares)
area.compHint: Open the address on a map, scan for the same kind of business within 1 km and enter them here. Mark each one’s strengths and weaknesses (read their reviews).
area.incAbove: Area income is {pct}% above the city average.
area.incBelow: Area income is {pct}% below the city average.
area.satNote: Counting you, each business gets about {people} people: {state}. This is a rough threshold; read it alongside foot traffic.
area.gapTitle: Where rivals are weak = your opening
area.gapNone: No shared weakness marked yet. Pick weaknesses on the competitor cards.
area.stakeTitle: Where everyone is strong = table stakes
area.stakeNone: No area where most rivals are strong.
area.stakeText: Do not open until you match rivals here; it will not set you apart, but falling short loses customers.

location.footHint: Count the people walking past the door in each slot, on one weekday and one weekend day. The app turns it into daily passers-by.
location.footInfo: This business runs by appointment: the foot count is shown for information and does not affect the score or red flags.
location.openHNote: Open hours come from the capacity section on the Financials tab.
location.rentHint: Rent comes from the rent rows on the Financials tab and sales from the base case. One number that tells you whether the spot is too expensive.
location.noRent: No rent row found in fixed costs.
location.histHint: Ask neighboring shop owners and the broker. A space that keeps changing hands points to a problem the numbers do not show.
location.lTurnover: Businesses that closed here in the last 5 years
location.lReason: Why did the last tenant leave?
location.lClosures: Same-sector closures nearby in the last 2 years
location.founderHint: The same shop is a different business when the owner runs it daily versus from a distance.
location.lRunway: Months you can go without a salary
location.lEquity: Share of investment from your own money (%)
location.mgrNote: If the owner is not on site every day, a manager salary is added to fixed costs automatically; half of it for part-time.
location.chkHint: Check each item in person. A "No" on a critical item is a red flag; unknowns go to the confirm list.
location.footDetail: About {daily} people pass by a day. Break-even needs {req} of them to come in; the base case needs {base}.
location.footBench: For this business, {good}% or less is comfortable and above {bad}% is a stretch.
location.rentBench: For this business, {good}% or less is healthy and above {bad}% is dangerous.

histNote.turnoverBad: 3+ businesses closed here in 5 years: the space may have a structural problem.
histNote.turnoverMid: 2 businesses closed here in 5 years; find out why.
histNote.noProfit: The last tenant left because it was not profitable. Learn why before you sign.
histNote.rent: The last tenant left over rent: negotiate the escalation clause.
histNote.closuresBad: 4+ same-sector businesses nearby closed in 2 years.
histNote.closuresMid: There have been same-sector closures nearby; find out why.

founderNote.manager: Owner is not on site daily; a manager salary was added and daily break-even moves {from} → {to}.
founderNote.years: No industry experience: work a few months in a similar shop before opening.
founderNote.runwayBad: You can go less than 3 months without a salary; you will end up pulling cash from the business early.
founderNote.runwayMid: You can go less than 6 months without a salary; the first months will be tight.
founderNote.equityBad: Most of the investment is debt; loan payments will eat your working capital.
founderNote.equityMid: The debt share is high; add loan payments to fixed costs.

location.talk: Talk to neighboring shops about the space’s history.

pricing.bandHint: Rival prices within 1 km and yours ({price}). The dashed line is the average.
pricing.posAt: You sit right at the average.
pricing.noPrices: Enter signature prices for competitors to compare.
pricing.stratHint: Each strategy shifts the whole menu by the same ratio. Volume is held at the base case: in reality premium brings fewer customers and penetration brings more.

cardDesc.pen: About 10% under the average. Wins customers fast, thins the margin.
cardDesc.match: Sit at the average and win on speed, experience and loyalty.
cardDesc.prem: About 15% over the average. Only if there is a quality gap you truly fill.

recWhy.prem: Most rivals look weak on quality; a premium position that fills that gap makes sense.
recWhy.pen: Most rivals are seen as pricey; pricing a little lower can pull customers through your door.
recWhy.match: No clear price or quality gap; staying at the average and winning on service is the safest call.
recWhy.sat: The area is saturated; avoid a price war, stay at the average and stand out on experience.
recWhy.incHi: Area income is well above the city average; it can carry a premium position.
recWhy.incLo: Area income is well below the city average; pricing a little under the average is safer.

pricing.beAbove: Break-even rises above your base case
pricing.floored: Some items were raised to the price floor
pricing.belowFloor: These items are priced below the floor: {items}. It does not change the verdict, but check the fee schedule.

tips.t1: Round prices consistently (e.g. 4.75, 5.25): the menu looks tidy and trustworthy.
tips.t2: Add an anchor item: the priciest option makes the middle one feel fair.
tips.t3: Bundle (coffee + pastry, cut + beard): bigger tickets, better margin.
tips.t4: A loyalty card beats a discount: a free 10th brings people back without cutting price.
tips.t5: When raising prices, move slow sellers first and your signature item last, in small steps.

storefront.sloganOff: Advertising is restricted in this profession, so the slogan field is off.
storefront.dlNote: First look: an instant sketch with your name and colors. Use it for thumbnails and pitches.

quick.title: Quick analysis
quick.lead: Your first verdict in 10 questions. Where you don't know, use the example figure from the video.
quick.resumed: You are picking up where you left off.

q.sector: What are you thinking of opening?
q.area: Which neighborhood is the shop in?
q.staff: What is the total monthly payroll?
q.role: How involved will you be day to day?
q.price: Your signature item: price and unit cost?
q.daily: How many {unit} do you expect a day?
q.capex: How much will you spend to open?
q.equity: How much of that is your own money?

hint.sector: The business type sets the thresholds and example figures the math uses.
hint.country: Tax, fee and loan defaults come from the country.
hint.area: An address or neighborhood name is enough.
hint.rent: Before rent withholding; the app adds it.
hint.staff: Total wages. The app adds employer payroll taxes. If you will work there yourself, list only the others.
hint.role: If you are not there every day, a manager salary is added to costs.
hint.price: Think of your best seller. Price as the customer pays it, cost before tax.
hint.daily: On a normal day. The app builds the pessimistic and optimistic cases from it.
hint.capex: Equipment, build-out, furniture, opening stock, permits. The app adds a contingency buffer.
hint.equity: The rest counts as a loan. Enter 100 if it is all your own money.

summary.title: First verdict
summary.confShare: Share based on example or estimated data: {pct}%
summary.confHint: These items come from the video example or country defaults. Enter your own figure, or tap "Correct" if the figure is right.
summary.confAll: Every item rests on your own data.
summary.preliminaryHint: More than half of this analysis rests on example or estimated data; do not read the verdict as final.

compare.candHint: Set up the same business for different shops and save each one. Every candidate keeps all of its data; load it to edit or compare side by side. Candidates are stored on this device.
compare.save: Save this analysis as a candidate
compare.max: You can save up to {max} candidates; delete one first.
compare.loadArm: This replaces the current analysis. Load?
compare.empty: No saved candidates yet. Finish the analysis for one shop, name it and save it; then do the same for the next shop.
compare.cmpHint: The best value in each row is highlighted (among candidates in the same currency).

report.heading: PDF report
report.hint: Puts the whole analysis in one file: verdict, numbers, 24-month projection, area, rivals, location scorecard, pricing strategy and the permit list. Share it with your bank, partner or family.
report.always: The investment notice, the permit notice and the last-reviewed date are in every report.
report.error: The report could not be created. Try again.
report.title: Feasibility report
report.stakes: Table stakes: where rivals are strong
report.disclaimer: This report comes from a teaching model and is not investment advice. The numbers rest on entered or sample data; check them with an accountant before you decide.

in.rampV: starts at {start}%, reaches base in {months} months

legal.title: Permit roadmap
legal.hint: A checklist of which documents you need and which authority issues them. This is not legal advice; mark each item for your own situation.
legal.warning: This list is a general guide and can change. Before you apply, confirm with your municipality, the relevant authority and your accountant. Last reviewed: {date}.
legal.draft: Draft items in this list have not been verified against an official source yet. Do not rely on them for an application.
legal.generic: We do not offer a permit list for this country. Ask your local municipality and accountant about permits and documents.
legal.none: There are no verified permit items for this business yet. Ask your municipality, the relevant authority and your accountant about permits and documents.

condition.hasSign: If you put up a sign

legal.openCritical: {count, plural, =0 {No critical items pending, as far as you have marked} one {# critical item not finished} other {# critical items not finished}}
legal.pathPartial: At least {min}–{max} days. The time for {count} items is not known yet, so it may take longer.
legal.pathUnknown: Could not be calculated: the time for {count} items has not been verified yet.
legal.pathNone: No items left that hold up opening.
legal.pathHint: The longest chain of items that wait on each other. Items that run at the same time are not added up.
legal.blocked: You marked "No" for the permit item in the location checklist, so the verdict is NO.
